subagent_reports.architecture_assessment: The design correctly diagnoses this as a documentation/help/test ambiguity, not a behavioral bug. Evidence confirms bin/adv:5 overstates the whole CLI as read-only while runDashboardInstall genuinely mutates (writes files + systemctl enable --now). The chosen approach — keep CLI shape, fix header/help/dry-run/README wording plus lock with tests — is the minimal boring solution and maps cleanly to all six ACs. Rejected alternatives (split binary, remove install, interactive confirm) are correctly declined: split/remove are heavier and constraint-violating; interactive confirm would change behavior/automation (violates C2/C5). No spec-law conflict: the advance-meta installer-authority law targets deploy-local.sh, not the dashboard install subcommand, and no new mutating CLI surface is added (respects C3). Server/systemd behavior is untouched beyond dry-run text (respects C2, AC6, rq-dashboardWorkerFree01). Two non-blocking gaps: (1) CLI surface matrix has no bin/adv dashboard-install row and design doesn't add one — matrix stays silent on the only mutating bin/adv subcommand though CI won't fail; (2) SETUP.md:1108 also describes the CLI but is neutral, so out-of-scope omission is acceptable.

validation.notes: Design is READY_WITH_NOTES. All six ACs are traceable to concrete file:line edits and are testable. Current tests do not lock the overstated wording, so AC2/AC3/AC5 changes will not collide with an unaccounted test. No spec-law conflict. Two non-blocking notes: consider adding a bin/adv dashboard-install disposition row to docs/cli-surface-matrix.md (it currently omits the only mutating bin/adv subcommand), and optionally align SETUP.md:1108 CLI description if the mutation boundary should be visible in the primary install doc. Neither is required to satisfy the approved contract.

tradeoffs: String/help/docs/test-only change keeps blast radius minimal but leaves the mutation boundary heuristic (prose in help/header) rather than structural — a reader who skips help can still invoke the mutating install; acceptable given the explicit 'install' verb + --dry-run already provide structural affordance.

Locking help/dry-run wording in tests prevents regression but couples test assertions to exact heading strings; mitigated by asserting stable substrings (e.g. 'MUTATION PLAN', 'No changes were made') rather than full output.
Not updating the CLI surface matrix keeps the change tightly scoped but leaves the governance matrix silent on the only mutating bin/adv subcommand.

alternatives_considered.option: Split dashboard install into a separate binary/command namespace
alternatives_considered.rationale: Heavier than needed; the explicit 'install' verb plus existing --dry-run already establish a structural boundary once wording is corrected. Would also expand scope beyond the clarity-only contract (C5).

alternatives_considered.option: Add interactive confirmation before install mutation
alternatives_considered.rationale: Changes runtime behavior and breaks automation/systemd install flows; violates C2 (no systemd behavior change beyond wording) and C5 (scope).

alternatives_considered.option: Add a bin/adv dashboard-install row to docs/cli-surface-matrix.md as part of this change
alternatives_considered.rationale: Improves governance completeness and is low-cost, but not required by any AC and CI does not enforce bin/adv subcommand matrix coverage. Surface as an optional in-scope campsite improvement or a follow-up, not a blocker.

documents.proposal:
# Clarify bin/adv command boundary

## Summary

Clarify `bin/adv` command boundaries so operator-facing text distinguishes read-only commands from mutating dashboard service installation.

## Problem

`bin/adv` identifies itself as a "Read-only terminal client" at the file header, but the same CLI contains `dashboard install`, which writes user config and systemd user service files, runs `systemctl --user daemon-reload`, and enables/starts the service. This creates a safety and operator-expectation mismatch: users and agents may treat the whole CLI as read-only even though one subcommand mutates local user state.

## Evidence

- `bin/adv:3-7` describes `adv` as a read-only terminal client.
- `bin/adv:412-423` creates directories, writes config/unit files, reloads systemd, and enables/starts a user service.
- `bin/adv:543-550` lists read/status commands next to `dashboard install`.
- `bin/adv:571-573` documents `--dry-run` for install/doctor, which implies mutation exists but the top-level framing still says read-only.
- `README.md:156` references `bin/adv dashboard install --profile pokeedge`.

## Why now

This is the second Epic entry after slop-scan correctness. Before optimizing or refactoring the CLI/status path, the command boundary should be explicit so future work preserves safe operator expectations.

## Intended outcome

A clear, tested CLI/documentation contract:

- Read-only commands remain clearly identified as read-only.
- Mutating dashboard installation is explicitly labeled as mutating local user state.
- Dry-run behavior remains available and documented for installation planning.
- Help/docs/tests no longer imply the entire CLI is read-only.

## Scope

- Inspect current `bin/adv` command/help text and dashboard install docs/tests.
- Update source comments/help/docs/tests to distinguish read-only vs mutating subcommands.
- Add or update tests that lock the boundary language.
- Keep implementation minimal unless discovery finds a real safety gap.

## Out of scope

- Removing `dashboard install`.
- Redesigning dashboard service management.
- Changing systemd behavior unless current help/docs are actively misleading about dry-run or mutation.
- Performance optimization work from later Epic entries.
- OCA-specific read-surface work.

## Epic context

Epic: `optimizeAdvPerformanceStructure`, entry 2.

Previous completed entry: `makeDegradedSlopScanFailFast` archived successfully.
documents.problemStatement:
## Problem

`bin/adv` has a command-boundary ambiguity: top-level source text says "Read-only terminal client", but `dashboard install` mutates local user state by writing dashboard config/service files and enabling a systemd user service.

## User-visible risk

Operators and agents may over-trust the CLI as read-only, then run a mutating subcommand without the expected mental model. This is especially risky because `dashboard install` affects user-level service configuration.

## Success Criteria

- Top-level CLI/help/docs no longer imply the whole `bin/adv` surface is read-only.
- Read-only subcommands and mutating subcommands are explicitly distinguished.
- `dashboard install` mutation targets and `--dry-run` safety path are clear in help/docs.
- Tests or asset checks lock the wording so the ambiguity does not regress.

# Agreement — Clarify bin/adv command boundary

## Discovery disposition

Current evidence supports a documentation/help/test ambiguity, not a behavioral bug. `bin/adv dashboard` itself is read-only, but `bin/adv dashboard install` is intentionally mutating. The problem is that the top-level CLI framing says the whole CLI is read-only.

## Evidence

- `bin/adv:3-7` describes `adv` as a "Read-only terminal client".
- `bin/adv:412-423` shows `dashboard install` creates directories, writes dashboard config/service files, runs `systemctl --user daemon-reload`, and runs `systemctl --user enable --now`.
- `bin/adv:543-550` lists read-only and mutating subcommands together.
- `bin/adv:571-573` documents `--dry-run` for install/doctor, but does not clearly label install as mutating.
- `README.md:149-169` documents local dashboard install and already lists write/systemctl targets.
- `bin/dashboard-cli.test.ts:105-121` covers install dry-run output and mutation plan lines.
- `docs/cli-surface-matrix.md:21-25` classifies `status`, `roadmap`, and `slop-scan` as CLI bridge/additive read/scanner surfaces, but does not describe `bin/adv dashboard install` as a mutating CLI subcommand.

## Objectives

1. Remove or qualify the misleading top-level "Read-only terminal client" framing.
2. Make `bin/adv --help` explicitly distinguish read-only commands from mutating dashboard install.
3. Make `dashboard install --dry-run` output clearly identify planned writes and systemctl actions before mutation.
4. Keep `dashboard` server itself documented as local read-only web UI.
5. Lock the wording with tests so future help/header changes do not regress the boundary.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: `bin/adv --help` includes a command-boundary statement that explicitly says most commands are read-only, while `dashboard install` mutates local user configuration/service state.
- AC2: The top-of-file CLI description no longer says or implies the entire `adv` CLI is read-only.
- AC3: `dashboard install --dry-run --profile pokeedge --home /home/example` output includes a clear mutation-plan heading and lists both file write targets and `systemctl --user` actions without performing them.
- AC4: README local dashboard docs explicitly identify `dashboard install` as the mutating install step and mention `--dry-run` as the preview path.
- AC5: Tests assert the help boundary language and dry-run mutation-plan language.
- AC6: Existing dashboard server behavior remains read-only and its help/docs still say local dashboard binds to loopback by default.

## Constraints

- Do not remove `dashboard install`.
- Do not change systemd install behavior except wording/output needed to clarify mutation boundaries.
- Do not add new mutating CLI surfaces.
- Do not introduce OCA-specific read-surface/API work.
- Keep change scoped to command-boundary clarity and tests.

## Out of scope

- Dashboard service redesign.
- Status/roadmap/slop-scan performance optimization.
- Archived listing timeout work.
- Status health-probe TTL work.
- Broader CLI architecture refactor.

# Design — Clarify `bin/adv` read/mutate boundary

## Decision

Keep the existing CLI shape and behavior. Fix the ambiguity through precise command-boundary wording, dry-run output wording, README wording, and tests.

No new command split is needed for this change because `dashboard install` already has `--dry-run`, an explicit `install` verb, and existing tests around planned writes. The bug is that top-level/help text overstates the entire CLI as read-only.

## Independent validation

`adv-researcher` verdict: `READY_WITH_NOTES`, confidence high, risk low.

Validator notes incorporated:

1. Tests should assert stable substrings (`MUTATION PLAN`, `No changes were made`) rather than full output equality.
2. Add a static/help test for AC2 so the header no longer claims the whole CLI is read-only.
3. Optional campsite: add a small `bin/adv` subcommand boundary section to `docs/cli-surface-matrix.md`; it is not required by existing matrix tests but improves discoverability.

## Implementation plan

### `bin/adv`

1. Replace the file header description:
   - from: "Read-only terminal client..."
   - to: wording that says status/roadmap/epic/list/dashboard reads are read-only, while `dashboard install` mutates local user service configuration.
2. Add a `COMMAND BOUNDARY` section in `runHelp()` before `SUBCOMMANDS`:
   - Most commands are read-only diagnostics/scanners.
   - `dashboard install` mutates local user state by writing config/unit files and enabling a systemd user service.
   - Use `dashboard install --dry-run` to preview writes/checks.
3. Update the `dashboard install` subcommand row to mention it is mutating.
4. Update `--dry-run` flag help from generic "planned writes/checks" to explicit preview-before-mutation wording.
5. Update `renderDashboardInstallPlan()` to start with a clear heading, e.g. `MUTATION PLAN: dashboard install` and `No changes were made (--dry-run).`, while preserving the existing file paths and systemctl commands.

### `README.md`

In Local dashboard section:

- Keep `bin/adv dashboard` documented as local read-only web dashboard.
- Label `bin/adv dashboard install --profile pokeedge` as the mutating install step.
- Add `--dry-run` preview example before the real install command.
- Keep existing write target and systemctl lists.

### `docs/cli-surface-matrix.md`

Add a compact `bin/adv` subcommand boundary section if it fits cleanly:

- read-only: `status`, `roadmap`, `slop-scan`, `epic list`, `dashboard`, `dashboard doctor`
- mutating local user state: `dashboard install`

This is campsite documentation only; do not expand into a larger CLI architecture matrix.

### Tests

Update `bin/dashboard-cli.test.ts`:

- Help test asserts command-boundary statement.
- Help test asserts `dashboard install` is marked mutating.
- Header/static test asserts the top file no longer claims the whole CLI is a "Read-only terminal client".
- Dry-run install test asserts mutation-plan heading and no-changes line using stable substrings.
- Existing path/systemctl assertions remain.

No runtime/systemd behavior changes are intended beyond dry-run text output.

## Contract mapping

- AC1: help test asserts explicit command-boundary statement.
- AC2: source/header static test asserts no whole-CLI read-only claim.
- AC3: dry-run test asserts mutation-plan heading, no-changes line, write targets, and systemctl actions.
- AC4: README edit labels install as mutating and shows dry-run preview.
- AC5: dashboard CLI tests lock help + dry-run wording.
- AC6: existing dashboard help still says local dashboard is read-only and default host is `127.0.0.1`; no server code changes.

## Alternatives considered

1. Split `dashboard install` into another binary.
   - Rejected: heavier than needed; `install` verb and `--dry-run` already provide a good boundary once wording is fixed.
2. Remove `dashboard install`.
   - Rejected by agreement constraint.
3. Require an interactive confirmation before install.
   - Rejected for now: would change behavior and automation; current scope is clarity/tests only.

## Risk

Low. Changes are string/help/docs/tests only, except dry-run output text. No real install behavior changes.

`bin/adv` now distinguishes read-only commands from mutating dashboard installation in source header, help output, dry-run output, README docs, AGENTS.md, and CLI surface docs.

## What changed

- Replaced top-of-file whole-CLI read-only wording with command-specific boundary language.
- Added `COMMAND BOUNDARY` help section.
- Marked `dashboard install` as a mutating install in help.
- Added explicit `MUTATION PLAN: dashboard install` and `No changes were made (--dry-run).` dry-run output.
- Updated README to show `--dry-run` preview before mutating install and identify local user config/service writes.
- Added compact `bin/adv` subcommand boundary section to `docs/cli-surface-matrix.md`.
- Updated AGENTS.md stale heading so developer-facing repo docs no longer call `bin/adv` read-only status CLI.
- Added tests for help boundary, header wording, dry-run mutation plan, and loopback/read-only dashboard wording.

## Verification

- `bun test bin/dashboard-cli.test.ts` — passed: 7 tests, 31 expects.
- `bun test bin/dashboard-cli.test.ts bin/adv.test.ts` — passed: 23 tests, 89 expects.
- `../bin/oc-test targeted -- src/cli-surface-matrix.test.ts` — passed: 2 tests.
- Static command verified old read-only header removed, help boundary present, dry-run mutation plan present, README dry-run preview present.
- Release harden stale wording searches passed: no `read-only status CLI`; `Read-only terminal client` appears only in a negative test assertion.

## Review

Acceptance reviewer verdict: `READY`; no findings and no changes made.

- Help/docs boundary wording present.
- Dry-run mutation plan wording present.
- Non-dry-run install behavior unchanged.

None for this change. Later Epic entries remain future work.
